summary: Wait for keeper retirement and bind proof cgroup ownership to the direct guardian.

rules.detail: No job admission or authorization changes.

compatibility.detail: Only the opt-in keeper lifecycle changes. The shared guardian exports its own PID together with the keeper path. The proof validates its direct supervising parent through /proc, the guardian command and opt-in parent argument, the supervisor marker, and the exact configured-parent/jobs-proof-<guardian-pid> path before accepting that keeper.

manual.detail: Stale or supplied keeper paths fail closed. Documentation states the accepted limit: an external SIGKILL, OOM kill or cgroup kill of the guardian itself cannot be cleaned up in-process. The printed leak-inspection command remains available.

recovery.detail: After reaping descendants, guardian cleanup writes cgroup.kill, polls cgroup.events for populated 0 for at most ten seconds, then removes the keeper. A timeout or cleanup error fails the run instead of racing asynchronous SIGKILL completion with an immediate rmdir.
